To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) deep learning models learn to approximate number systems for quantifiers; (b) these systems have the same properties as number systems found in humans; (c) the effectiveness of these systems is impeded by confounding factors, such as spatial arrangement, and thus, the model's performance is not a reliable proxy for the human performance.

(1) the approximate number system is a viable explanation for the behavior of FiLM on the most task, (2) the approximate number is not a perfect system, (3) the performance of the approximate number system declines with more difficult questions and (4) the approximate number can be confounded by spatial arrangement.
the FiLM model learns a system of approximate number which is sensitive to spatial arrangement of the visual scene, and that this system is consistent with the Weber-Fechner law.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question of what cognitive processes underlie the performance of visual question answering models.
the question of what deep learning models for image captioning and question answering learn and how their performance can be interpreted.
the question of how models for visual question-answering learn the semantics of natural language quantifiers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FiLM learns to approximate a form of approximate numerical cognition which is not robust enough to be applied to real-world images.
the model learns a form of approximate counting which is not sufficient for the task of answering "most" questions.
the FiLM model learns a form of approximate numerosity, which is not sufficient to solve the task.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
deep learning models for image captioning and visual question answering are not yet able to learn a concept of "most" that is comparable to the one that humans have.
the FiLM visual model is not yet capable of learning the cognitive concepts of the approximate number system.
the FiLM architecture learns a strategy that is consistent with the approximate number system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current state-of-the-art in visual question answering models for quantifier statements is still far from human-like reasoning abilities.
deep learning models for image understanding are not yet at a level of cognitive complexity that is needed to interpret quantifiers in a scene.
the FiLM model learns an approximate number system for the quantifier "most" which can be explained in terms of Weber's law.
